description:
FILED s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5).  PRE-EXISTING and SILENT -- there is
no drop announcement, no `;; PARSE ERROR`, and no census row: the statement
simply is not in the emitted CL.  A #138-family member no instrument counts.

  no strict 'refs';
  my $one = "1";
  local *{"1"} = sub { 123 };
  print "x=[", &$one(), "]\n";

  perl: x=[123]
  PCL emits:
      (let (($one "1"))
        (p-print "x=[" (p-list-ctx (p-funcall-ref $one)) "]"))
  -- the local line is GONE; the run dies "Undefined subroutine &main::1 called".

WITHOUT `local` the same statement is fine (`*{"1"} = sub { 123 }` emits
`p-glob-assign-dynamic` and prints 123), so the loss is in the `local` path.

CAUSE, located: `Pl::Parser::_process_local_declaration` (~Pl/Parser.pm:3613)
enters its typeglob branch only when

    ref($non_ws[0]) eq 'PPI::Token::Symbol' && $non_ws[0]->content =~ /^\*(.+)$/

so a `*{EXPR}` target -- a Token::Cast('*') followed by a Structure::Block --
never matches, and nothing downstream claims it either.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: s446k's #463 repair rewrites `*1` into `*{'1'}`, so
`local *1 = sub {â¦}` (t/op/method.t:38, t/op/tie_fetch_count.t:203) would have
become this silent loss.  `local` is therefore deliberately NOT in the
repair's position whitelist (`Pl::Parser2::_glob_name_position`) and that
shape keeps DROPPING LOUDLY until this task closes -- at which point the
whitelist gains `local` and the guard row in `Pl/t/punct-glob-name-01.t`
becomes a both_agree on `local *1 = sub { 123 }`.

SHAPE: a `p-local-glob-dynamic` runtime macro (save/restore all slots of a
glob named at RUN time) plus the branch in _process_local_declaration.  FIRST,
rule 12: the fall-through must ANNOUNCE rather than vanish -- that half is
worth doing on its own even before the feature, and it is how this bug should
have been visible.

MEASURED s446k, and it is WIDER than the `*{EXPR}` spelling: the RAW form is
lost the same way and has never been a census row.

  no strict 'refs'; my $one = "1";
  my @res = eval { local *1 = sub { 123 }; &$one() };

  `./pl2cl` announces NOTHING and emits NO `;; PARSE ERROR`; the local line is
  simply absent.  t/op/method.t:38 and t/op/tie_fetch_count.t:203 are exactly
  this, and the census counts ONE drop in method.t -- a different statement.

So the fall-through in _process_local_declaration swallows every `local` whose
first non-whitespace part is not a Token::Symbol/subscript shape it knows, and
that is the half to fix FIRST (rule 12: announce, do not vanish).  Only then
does the feature (`p-local-glob-dynamic`) make sense, and only then does
`local` join Pl::Parser2::_glob_name_position's whitelist.
subject: `local *{EXPR} = â¦` loses the WHOLE STATEMENT silently -- _process_local_declaration's typeglob branch matches a Token::Symbol only, and a Cast+Block target falls through to nothing
